blocks.text: Violation tickets help track, investigate, and resolve policy violations discovered in Asset Exposure Management (AEM). To support different remediation workflows, you can manage violation tickets in several ways, including splitting unrelated policy violations from an existing violation ticket into one or more new tickets, and merging multiple violation tickets into a single ticket. These actions help you organize the remediation work and keep all related context in one place.

You can split policy violations from a violation ticket into one or more new tickets. For example, if a violation ticket contains multiple unrelated policy violations, you can split them into separate tickets so each violation is tracked and resolved independently.
To split violations from an existing violation ticket into a new ticket:

blocks.item: In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Assets in the top navigation bar.
In the left-side navigation, click Violation Tickets.
The Violation Tickets page appears.
See image.
Click the violation ticket you want to split.
The ticket details drawer opens.
Click the Policy Violations tab.
Select the policy violations you want to split.
See image.

To select all the policy violations on the current page, select the checkbox at the top of the list. Use the pagination controls to move to other pages and select additional policy violations. At least one of the selected policy violations must be active; inactive selections cannot be split.
The Split Into a New Violation Ticket drop-down menu appears.
From the drop-down menu, select one of the following options:
Split Into a New Violation Ticket: Split all policy violations into one ticket.
Split Into <#> New Violation Tickets: Create separate tickets for each policy violation.
See image.
A dialog window appears.
In the dialog window:
Assignee: Enter the user responsible for reviewing or resolving the violation ticket.
Status: Select the current state of the ticket (e.g., New, Open, In Progress, etc.).
See image.
Click Split.

A dialog window appears in the bottom-right corner of the page, where you can click and view the split ticket when processing is complete. When the process is complete, click View Ticket to review your newly split ticket. You can view the original ticket from which policy violations were split on the Related Tickets tab of your newly created ticket.

blocks.text: You can merge violation tickets when you want to combine tickets with related findings into a single ticket. A common use case for merging violation tickets is when multiple violation tickets contain similar policy violations that can be resolved with the same fix. Merging them creates a single work item that is easier to assign, track, and remediate.
To merge multiple violation tickets into one single ticket:

blocks.item: In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Assets in the top navigation bar.
In the left-side navigation, click Violation Tickets.
The Violation Tickets page appears.
Select the violation tickets you want to merge.
Click Merge.
See image.
A dialog window opens.
In the dialog window:
Assignee: Enter the name of the user responsible for reviewing or resolving the violation ticket.
Status: Select a status for the new ticket (e.g., New, Open, In Progress, etc.).
See image.
Click Merge.
A dialog window appears in the bottom-right corner of the page, indicating the merge process. When the process is complete, click View Ticket to review your newly merged ticket.
